summary: DHARA C1 greeting/capability fix + suggestion chips verified. Backend live SSE (public URL, authenticated): 'hi', 'what is dhara', 'thanks', 'who are you', 'नमस्ते'(hi), 'what can you do' all return the exact C1 template in 3 frames [session, delta, done] in 1.3-4.2s, with no status/LLM path, no citations and no 'cannot confirm' refusal. Extra edge cases also pass: 'Hi Dhara', 'hey dhara, good evening', 'What is DHARA?', 'धारा क्या है'(hi), 'Hello'(hi), 'hi'(ta). Deny list works: 'help me' is NOT intercepted and falls through to the legal pipeline. The helmet question returns a real answer (Rs 1,000 fine + 3-month licence suspension) with 2-3 citations. All 4 basic chips were sent to the backend in EN and 2 in HI. All are answerable with citations and none are refused. Unit suite tests/test_c1_conversational_intents.py: 50/50 pass. Frontend (375x667): language -> consent -> login -> Home -> 'Type' -> chat. The empty state shows exactly 4 legal chips (cheque bounce, UPI fraud, helmet fine, child pillion helmet) and no meta-questions. Typing 'hi' and 'what is dhara' renders the template in a chat bubble with no refusal. Tapping chip suggestion-2 gives a real helmet answer. Profile-specific and pro chip sources (userProfile.ts, PRO_SUGGESTIONS) also contain only legal questions. No deprecated Expo packages detected.

minor.issue: Deny list works as designed, but the fall-through reply is non-deterministic and often cold. Across 3 runs, 2 replies were 'I cannot confirm this from the official text. Please consult an advocate.' and 1 was an LLM clarification ('I need more information to help you...'). 'help me' can be a distress cue, so a refusal is poor UX. Consider a deterministic safety/clarify reply for deny-listed short messages (e.g. emergency numbers 112/1091 plus 'tell me what happened') rather than the corpus refusal.

guest_question_count is incremented (chat_router.py ~line 368) before the C1 gate (~line 1358). A guest saying 'hi' or 'thanks' therefore uses up one of their 5 free questions. Move the increment after the C1 short-circuit, or skip it when a C1 template is returned.

The C1 gate runs only after the full pre-retrieval and retrieval pipeline, so a canned greeting still takes 1.3-4.2s. It is functionally correct, but the gate could run earlier for speed (after the emergency check).

Not C1-related. The answer to 'Money gone in a UPI fraud — what do I do first?' has the wrong actor: 'the perpetrator must file a complaint immediately with your bank and the police.' It should be the victim (you). Possibly an actor-conduct reframing bug.

Not C1-related. 'hi, my cheque bounced what can I do' is correctly NOT intercepted, but it returns the 'cannot confirm from the official text' refusal, while the cheque-bounce chip question is answered fine. A greeting prefix seems to hurt retrieval.

issues: Tapping tab-ask auto-starts mic recording (URL ?autostartMic=). The locked-rec-bar then covers the chip list (chips 1-3 sit underneath it) and hides chat-input until cancelled. This is pre-existing behaviour and not part of this change; text chat is reachable via the Home 'Type' button.

action_items: (Optional/UX) Give deny-listed short messages like 'help me' a deterministic safety/clarification reply instead of the corpus 'cannot confirm' refusal.
Do not count C1 template replies against the guest_question_count quota.
Investigate the actor error in the UPI-fraud answer ('the perpetrator must file a complaint...').
(Optional) Strip a leading greeting before retrieval so 'hi, my cheque bounced...' is answered rather than refused.
critical_code_review_comments: conversational_intents.py: the raw_lower fallback is safe. It runs under the same length cap, action veto and anchored patterns, and only adds matches where the vocative stripper removed 'dhara' as an object.
The C1 gate correctly sits after the _emergency check and the is_denylisted() check, and returns before early_refusal and the LLM path.
frontend i18n home.suggestion1-4 has no 'gu' translation, although gu is a C1-verified language. It presumably falls back to English.
Live test file reads EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. frontend/.env has no EXPO_BACKEND_URL key, only EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the live tests with: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_c1_greeting_stream_live.py -n 0 -v (pytest.ini adds -n xdist). CITATION_GUARD_ENABLED=true, so legal answers arrive in a 'final' frame, not in deltas. UI path: language-screen (lang-en, language-continue) -> consent (consent-age-adult, consent-terms-checkbox, consent-data-checkbox, consent-continue-button) -> login -> /home. Dismiss the 'Continue in English' sheet, then tap the 'Type' text to open chat with chat-input and suggestion-0..3. tab-ask auto-starts the mic.
rca_of_issue: The original bug was that greetings went to corpus retrieval and got refused. It is fixed by the C1 gate. The 'what is dhara' miss happened because the _VOCATIVE_RE stripper removed 'dhara', leaving 'what is'. The raw_lower fallback match fixes this, and it was verified live.
